Week 1 is in the books, and we already have our first family feud. Will put up 162.7, the second-best score in the league, and still took the L because little brother Tom dropped the week's high score on him, 197.2. Igor Shesterkin led all goalies with 23.7 for Tom, and yes, that includes a goal to go with an assist. Not bad for a team that went 3-17 a year ago.

Reigning back-to-back champ Jefe opens the three-peat bid with a stumble. Joe squeaks past him 119.5 to 116.8, the closest game of the week. Jefe had won five of their six meetings coming in, so maybe it's just rust. Elsewhere in the family, Danny gets his revenge on sister-in-law Hallie for last year, 156.1 to 132.4, and hands her an IOU on that Bruins/Rangers punishment 😉

Rough start for Vin, the only manager who didn't crack triple digits (78.3). Calgary is off to an ugly start, Martone is easing into his rookie year, and Aleksander Barkov is now out 10-12 weeks. Worse, the loss came to Zac. You'd think he'd know that lineup.

Elias Pettersson led all forwards with 33.3 for Will, and Evan Bouchard paced the D with 26.2 for Zac. Darcy Kuemper had a week to forget for Tim at -3.8. Up next: Jefe tries to shake the rust against Ronnie, and Tom takes his 1-0 start into a matchup with sister-in-law Hallie.
Well, the rust is gone. Jefe answers his opening loss with 195.6 points, the week's high score, a 30.7-point win over Ronnie, and a jump from 11th to 4th. The champ is back in the conversation.

Tom stays perfect, but only just. He gets past sister-in-law Hallie 123.5 to 122.6, a 0.9-point escape and the closest game of the week. Expect that one to come up at the next family dinner 👀 Danny and Steve join him at 2-0, and Danny's 40.1-point rout of Zac was the biggest win of the week.

Somebody check on Will. He's 0-2 with the second-most points in the league (316.3), and Nick handed him this week's loss, 164.7 to 153.6. Hallie is 0-2 as well, so it's a quiet week in that household. Vin joins them after Tim beat him 146.6 to 120.7.

Star of the week: Tim Stutzle, 31.8 for Nick. Jake Oettinger stood on his head for Danny with 26.8. The waiver wire never slept, with 23 moves, including Jefe cutting Alex Ovechkin and Tom letting Igor Shesterkin walk one week after his goal. Up next: brother vs. brother, as Tim gets a shot at Danny's 2-0 start. Danny has won four of their six all-time meetings.
Brother vs. brother went to Tim. He takes the high-score crown with 191.9 and hands Danny his first loss of the season, 191.9 to 166.6.

Tom keeps rolling: 182.9 over Nick, his first win over Nick in seven tries, 3-0, and the last unbeaten team standing. Ronnie knocked Steve from the unbeaten ranks by 39.2, and Vin finally gets in the win column, edging Joe 124.1 to 119.0.

The headline performance of the young season: Brady Tkachuk, 41.0 for Vin, the best skater week yet. But Vin lived at both ends of the stat sheet, also rostering the week's lowest defenseman (Luca Cagnoni, -0.7) and goalie (Sergei Murashov, -3.2). Seth Jones led the D with 26.8 for Tim.

Trouble at the bottom, and it's all under one roof: Will and Hallie both fall to 0-3. Zac beat Hallie again, too, and is now 7-0 against her all-time. Nick was working the phones all week with six moves. Up next: Tom takes his perfect record into Zac, and Will gets Steve in search of a first win.
We have a new number one. Jefe drops 188.2 on Nick for the week's high score, his second of the season, a third straight win, and the top spot in the standings. Let the three-peat talk begin.

Upset alert: Zac, 7th coming in, takes down the unbeaten Tom 156.3 to 120.0, and Tom slides from 1st to 4th. Zac is now 5-1 all-time against Tom. Photo finish of the week goes to Hallie, who edges brother-in-law Tim 179.0 to 178.1 to snap a three-game skid. Blowout of the week: Ronnie over Vin by 65.0.

Leon Draisaitl led all skaters with 32.2 for Hallie. Jacob Trouba (20.7, Joe) and Joel Hofer (22.0, Ronnie) topped the D and G. And the first trade of the season stays in the family: Danny sends Stuart Skinner to brother Tim for Andrei Svechnikov. The league office is reviewing the tape 👀 Meanwhile, Vin snatched Jake Sanderson off waivers a day after Tim cut him loose.

Game of the week: Jefe (1st) vs. Tom (4th), both 3-1, with the top spot on the line. History is on Jefe's side: he is 6-0 all-time against Tom, including a 257.3 to 212.9 win in week 15 last season. Will draws Vin, who is 1-3 himself and 4-2 against Will all-time, in another shot at that first win.
